codex.variables.name: Variables
codex.variables.happened: The attack was {expression}. With your numbers filled in: {filled} = {value}.
codex.int-truncation.name: Integer truncation
codex.int-truncation.happened: {before} damage hit {enemy:target}, an int. An int has no room for decimals, so they were cut off: {after}.
codex.integer-division.name: Integer division
codex.integer-division.happened: {expression} gave {value}. When both sides are int, C# throws the remainder away: 7 / 2 is 3, not 3.5.
codex.overflow.name: Integer overflow
codex.overflow.happened: {enemy:target} was a {type} with {before} HP. Adding {added} made it {after}: a {type} can't go past {max}, so it wrapped around.
codex.operator-precedence.name: Operator precedence
codex.operator-precedence.happened: The Reckoner hid his totals. {expression} is {value}, because * goes before +.
codex.string-concat.name: String concatenation
codex.string-concat.happened: {expression} became {value}. With text, + glues instead of adding.
codex.string-length.name: String length
codex.string-length.happened: The text was {length} characters long. Every character counts: "6" is one, "2.5" is three, and a space counts too.
codex.char-is-number.name: A char is a number
codex.char-is-number.happened: {expression} gave {value}. Every char is a number: 'A' is 65, and the character '0' is 48, not 0.
codex.casting.name: Casting
codex.casting.happened: You remolded {enemy:target} from {from} to {to}: {before} became {after}. Remolding has a real name: casting.
codex.convert.name: Convert
codex.convert.happened: {expression} gave {value}. Convert rounds .5 to the nearest even number, and it checks: a value that doesn't fit throws an exception instead of wrapping.
codex.rounding.name: Math.Round
codex.rounding.happened: {before} damage on {enemy:enemy} became {after}. Math.Round sends .5 to the nearest even number: 2.5 is 2, 3.5 is 4.
codex.parse.name: Parsing
codex.parse.happened: {text} gave {value}. Text that looks like a number is still text, until you parse it.
codex.exceptions.name: Exceptions
codex.exceptions.happened: {expression} threw a {exception}. The code compiled fine, but crashed while it ran.
bug.golem.title: Pac-Man, level 256 (1980)
bug.golem.story: Pac-Man kept the level number in a single byte. After level 255 came 256, which a byte cannot hold. The game drew half the maze from garbage memory, and nobody could finish it.
bug.effective-power.title: Effective Power (iPhone, 2015)
bug.effective-power.story: One text message could crash any iPhone that received it. It held a short run of Arabic and other Unicode characters that the phone's text layout couldn't handle. The moment the message appeared in a notification, the phone tried to draw it and crashed, over and over. This one crashes too, once its text gets long enough.
bug.counter.title: Gangnam Style (YouTube, 2014)
bug.counter.story: YouTube counted views in a 32-bit int. Gangnam Style got so popular that its counter crept toward 2,147,483,647, the largest number an int can hold. One more and it would have wrapped around to minus two billion. YouTube switched to a 64-bit counter just in time. This counter wasn't so lucky.
bug.colossus.title: Ariane 5, flight 501 (1996)
bug.colossus.story: Ariane 5 reused software from the smaller Ariane 4. A speed value that fit fine on the old rocket was too large for its new, smaller type. The conversion failed, the guidance shut down, and the rocket destroyed itself 37 seconds after launch.
bug.index.title: Vancouver Stock Exchange (1982)
bug.index.story: A new stock index started at 1000. It was recalculated thousands of times a day, and every time the result was cut off after three decimals instead of rounded. Each cut lost a tiny bit. After 22 months the index stood at about 520, while its real value was over 1000.
event.foundry.title: The Foundry
event.foundry.text: You wake beside a forge that is still warm. Three things lie on the anvil, but you can only carry one.
event.foundry.card.detail: Choose 1 of 3 uncommon or rare cards.
event.foundry.relic.outcome: {relic:relic} is yours. The forge hisses as you leave.
event.foundry.gold.detail: Spend it in a shop, or on removing a card.
event.foundry.gold.outcome: The pouch is heavier than it looks.
event.crucible.title: The Crucible
event.crucible.text: A crucible full of molten metal bubbles over a fire. Whatever goes in comes out in a different shape.
event.crucible.pour.detail: It costs 0 from now on, but loses its decimals.
event.crucible.pour.outcome: You pour {card:from} into the crucible. Out comes {card:to}: free, but without decimals.
event.crucible.melt.detail: Remove a card from your deck. Lose {amount} HP.
event.crucible.melt.outcome: The crucible swallows {card:card}. The fire scorches your hand.
event.leaking-barrel.title: The Leaking Barrel
event.leaking-barrel.text: Gold drips from a crack in an enormous barrel. The barrel creaks dangerously.
event.leaking-barrel.catch.outcome: You catch the gold. Then the barrel bursts and knocks you flat.
event.leaking-barrel.leave.detail: The barrel keeps creaking behind you.
event.copy-machine.title: The Copy Machine
event.copy-machine.text: A copy machine hums in a corner, far too hot to touch. The manual says: never copy a card. Under it, someone scribbled: why not?
event.copy-machine.copy.detail: Add an exact copy to your deck. Lose {amount} HP.
event.copy-machine.copy.outcome: Out slides a second {card:card}, still warm. So are your fingers.
event.scrap-bin.title: The Scrap Bin
event.scrap-bin.text: A bin full of parts that didn't pass inspection. Nobody will notice one more. Or one less.
event.scrap-bin.toss.detail: Remove a card from your deck. Free.
event.scrap-bin.toss.outcome: {card:card} lands on the pile with a clang.
event.scrap-bin.dig.outcome: Between the bolts you find a handful of coins.
event.rounding-desk.title: The Rounding Desk
event.rounding-desk.text: A clerk with a stamp offers to tidy up your purse. "Nobody likes loose change," he says. "I round to the nearest hundred. Math.Round, very fair."
event.rounding-desk.round.outcome: Stamp. {gold} became {rounded}. At exactly .5 he rounds to the even number, very fair indeed.

ui.subtitle: Act 1: The Vat Valley
ui.tagline: A deckbuilder where the world obeys C#.
ui.intro.title: Not by the manual
ui.intro.1: The factory builds everything by the specification. You are the little figure from its assembly manual.
ui.intro.2: The manual is full of crossed-out panels: things you must never do. But the manual is only paper. The world obeys C#, and C# allows a lot more.
ui.intro.3: Nobody will explain the rules. Bump into them, bend them, break them. The Codex will tell you their names later.

ui.world.card-hall.name: The Card Hall
ui.world.card-hall.text: Cards, vats and molds: values, text and types. Where it all started.
ui.world.control-room.name: The Control Room
ui.world.control-room.text: Set the rules, then watch the machine work. The first rule that fits, wins. A prototype for now.

ui.reveal.title: The wall cracks open
ui.reveal.won: Behind the Card Hall, the factory goes on. More departments, more chapters, more rules to break. And you've been building it all along.
ui.reveal.crack: You've come here often enough. Something gave way behind the wall. The factory is bigger than the Card Hall.
ui.reveal.crack-button: There's a crack in the wall
ui.account.title: Your factory
ui.account.keep.text: Pick a name and a password. Then you can play on with your factory on any computer.
ui.account.login.text: Already kept your factory somewhere else? Log in to bring it here. What you did on this computer comes along.
ui.account.name: Username or email
ui.account.with-email: With an email address, you can get a new password if you forget it. We never send you anything else.
ui.account.without-email: Without an email address, nobody can help you if you forget your password. Your factory is then gone for good.
ui.account.signed-in: Your factory is kept. You log in as {name}.
ui.account.nickname: Others see you as {nickname}. Nobody ever sees your username.
ui.account.error.offline: No connection right now. Your factory is safe on this computer; try again later.
ui.account.error.taken: That name is already taken. Try another one.
ui.account.error.wrong-login: That name and password don't match.
ui.account.error.bad-name: A username has 3 to 20 letters, digits, - or _. Or type a whole email address.
ui.account.error.short-password: A password needs at least 8 characters.
ui.account.error.unknown-code: There is no class with that code.
ui.account.error.bad-class-name: A class name has 1 to 60 characters.
ui.account.error.failed: That didn't work. Try again later.
ui.tease.rattle: Behind the door marked 5, something rattles.
act.vat-valley.flavor: Everything here is a value in a vat, and every vat has a shape. Pour in what doesn't fit, and see what happens.
act.mold-works.flavor: Molten metal, poured into molds. Here every value gets forced into a new type, and not everything survives the trip.
act.print-shop.flavor: Loose letters in wooden cases, waiting to be set. Every letter is a number, and every sentence is longer than it looks.
